title: Generalized Additive Models (GAMs)
interviewAnswer: GAMs add flexible smooth functions of individual predictors while retaining an additive, interpretable structure. They are useful when relationships are nonlinear but black-box complexity is unnecessary.
keyPoints: Additivity is interpretable but limits interactions unless added explicitly.
why: Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Additivity is interpretable but limits interactions unless added explicitly.
deepDive: GAMs add flexible smooth functions of individual predictors while retaining an additive, interpretable structure. They are useful when relationships are nonlinear but black-box complexity is unnecessary. Smoothness must be controlled. Works with generalized response families. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Model conversion probability as smooth functions of price and tenure plus categorical device effects.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) make?
How would you validate or debug Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
